title: Graph of the derivative: extrema, concavity and a tangent line

stimulus.title: The graph of $f'$, the derivative of $f$
stimulus.text: The function $f$ is defined and differentiable on the closed interval $[-4, 5]$. The graph of $f'$, the derivative of $f$, consists of a semicircle below the $x$-axis from $x = -4$ to $x = 0$ and two line segments, from $(0, 0)$ to $(2, 3)$ and from $(2, 3)$ to $(5, -3)$. It is given that $f(2) = 5$.

plot.label: Graph of f prime on the closed interval from -4 to 5: a semicircle of radius 2 below the x-axis from (-4, 0) to (0, 0) with lowest point (-2, -2), a segment from (0, 0) up to (2, 3), and a segment from (2, 3) down through (3.5, 0) to (5, -3)

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the $x$-coordinate of each point at which $f$ has a relative minimum and each point at which $f$ has a relative maximum on the open interval $-4 < x < 5$. Justify your answers.

rubric.point: Relative minimum at $x = 0$, with the reason: $f'$ changes from negative to positive at $x = 0$
accept: the reason must name $f'$ and the direction of its sign change; "$f'(0) = 0$" alone earns nothing

rubric.point: Relative maximum at $x = 3.5$, with the reason: $f'$ changes from positive to negative at $x = 3.5$

parts.sample: $f$ has a relative minimum at $x = 0$, because $f'$ changes from negative to positive there. $f$ has a relative maximum at $x = \frac{7}{2}$, because $f'$ changes from positive to negative there. (On $[2, 5]$, $f'(x) = 7 - 2x$, which is zero at $x = 3.5$.)

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the open intervals on which the graph of $f$ is concave down. Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.point: Reason: $f'$ is decreasing on those intervals
accept: "$f''(x) < 0$ there" when tied to the graph of $f'$ falling
the reason must be about $f'$ decreasing, not about $f'$ being negative

parts.sample: The graph of $f$ is concave down on $(-4, -2)$ and on $(2, 5)$, because $f'$ is decreasing on those intervals.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the $x$-coordinate of each point of inflection of the graph of $f$ on $-4 < x < 5$. Justify your answer.

accept: both values with no extra values such as $x = 0$ or the zeros of $f'$

rubric.point: Justification: $f'$ changes from decreasing to increasing at $x = -2$ and from increasing to decreasing at $x = 2$
accept: not earned by "$f'$ changes sign" or by zeros of $f'$

parts.sample: The graph of $f$ has points of inflection at $x = -2$ and $x = 2$. At $x = -2$, $f'$ changes from decreasing to increasing, and at $x = 2$, $f'$ changes from increasing to decreasing, so the concavity of $f$ changes at both. ($f'$ is increasing on both sides of $x = 0$, so there is no inflection point there.)

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of $f$ at $x = 2$. Use it to approximate $f(2.2)$. Is this approximation an overestimate or an underestimate of $f(2.2)$? Explain your reasoning.

rubric.point: Overestimate, because the graph of $f$ is concave down on $(2, 2.2)$ ($f'$ is decreasing there), so it lies below its tangent line
accept: the reason must use concavity on the interval to the right of $x = 2$

parts.sample: $f'(2) = 3$ from the graph, so the tangent line is $y = 5 + 3(x - 2)$. Then $f(2.2) \approx 5 + 3(0.2) = 5.6$. On $(2, 5)$, $f'$ is decreasing, so the graph of $f$ is concave down there and lies below its tangent line. The approximation $5.6$ is an overestimate.
